cross_lane_assumptions: Lane 1: browser.web.read observed keeps {final_url, source_sha256, document_id, page_revision, authority DATA_ONLY}; recipes bind only these fields, never assumed body text

Lane 2: desktop.open payload {process_id, application, target, idempotency_key} and desktop.control.assert payload {window: {process_id}, value} are the expected contract; convergence may rename fields without engine changes
Lane 2: desktop legs need a real owned desktop session; no desktop proof attempted in this sandbox
Lane 3: git.push needs an owned disposable remote; absolute-path remotes were refused/honestly-failed in this sandbox, so push stays sibling-proven
Lane 3: github.pull_request.publish provider-readback legs untouched by this lane
likely_conflicts: Lanes 1-3 may also touch src/jarvis_foundry/fabric/loop.py seed_builtins if they add capabilities; merge is additive (capability list), keep cap.workflow.run entry
If a sibling edits compose.run_workflow result shaping, preserve new keys outcome/resumed_steps/soft_failed_steps/checkpoint used by recipes/runner
If a sibling edits WorkflowStep.on_failure validation, preserve soft|optional|retry values
integration_order_notes: Land this lane's fabric/recipes + compose/loop/executors/CLI changes first (additive, backward compatible: existing run_workflow callers unaffected)
Then bind Lane 1 browser readback field names if they differ (recipes only reference final_url/source_sha256/document_id)
Then bind Lane 2 desktop payload field names for open/assert steps
Then run v14.digital_operator.close live against disposable remote + desktop session for LIVE_PROOF_LATER closure
next_highest_value_work: Live v14.digital_operator.close proof with Lane 1 browser + Lane 2 desktop session + Lane 3 disposable remote (needs convergence, not this lane alone)
github.pull_request.publish variant of v14.publish_verified_work once Lane 3 readback transport is converged
Checkpoint aging/GC policy for long-lived recipes (currently sidecars persist until replaced; no TTL)
